text:
Rafael Mendes: Need SRE eyes on the proposed paging thresholds for the auto-rollback SLO breach work. Main concern: flapping + noisy pages during canary warm-up / low traffic. Draft notes here: https://confluence.redwood/platform/rollouts/auto-rollback-alerting (wip). What should page vs ticket? What cooldown/min-traffic defaults do we want?

Aisha Bello: +1 on flapping risk. If we page on “breach detected” we’ll page on every transient spike (esp dedicated tenants w/ bursty traffic). I’d rather page only when (a) rollback executed OR (b) breach persists beyond 2 eval intervals and rollback is blocked (policy off, monitor unknown, cooldown, etc.).

Sean Gallagher: Agree. Separate “controller took action” from “monitor saw something.”
- Event stream: always emit breach + verdict for audit.
- Paging: only for ACTIONABLE or “couldn’t protect customer.”
Also: thresholds shouldn’t be absolute only. Need baseline compare or burn-rate style.

Benji Okafor: From controller side we can expose a `verdict` state + reason in the event: `healthy | breached | breached_worse_than_baseline | unknown | insufficient_traffic | cooldown_active`.
If you tell us what should drive a page, we can make incident-bot only page on those.

Allison Grant: Strong preference: “must-be-worse-than-baseline” check, otherwise you roll back for global incidents that hit both baseline + canary equally (network, upstream deps, bad region). If canary and stable both degrade, rollback doesn’t help.
Proposed: compare canary p95 latency / error-rate vs stable over same window; require canary worse by X%.

Miles Thornton: +1. We’ve been burned by “global degradation triggers mass rollback” before.
For anti-flap:
- minimum traffic threshold (requests + tokens) before any decision
- warm-up grace period after rollout step (no rollback decisions for N minutes)
- cooldown after rollback (per {tenant, route, region}) so we don’t bounce back/forth

Rafael Mendes: On defaults, I was thinking:
- warm-up grace: 5 min after traffic split changes
- min traffic: 200 req OR 100k tokens in window (whichever first)
- eval window: 10 min rolling
- cooldown: 30 min
Does that sound sane or too strict?

Sean Gallagher: 5 min grace is ok, but min-traffic needs to scale w/ tier. Hosted small routes will never hit 200 req in 10m and then we’ll never protect them.
Maybe default on “min req” but allow per-route override + a floor like 30 req. Also consider “two-window confirm”:
- breach must happen in 2 consecutive windows (e.g., 5m + 10m) before rollback
This reduces one-off spikes without making you wait forever.

Aisha Bello: Another idea: for error rate, use consecutive windows; for latency, compare to baseline and require sustained delta.
Example (numbers illustrative):
- latency: canary p95 > max(absolute_threshold, 1.25x stable_p95) for 2 windows
- errors: canary 5xx rate > max(0.5%, 2x stable_5xx) for 2 windows
We should avoid paging on the first 5xx burst during deploy.

Jordan Lee: Policy engine can encode “must be worse than baseline” as a boolean + `baseline_delta_pct`.
Question: baseline should be previous stable *version* on same route/region, right? Or an SLO target constant?

Allison Grant: Baseline should be stable version on same route/region/tier if available. If stable has near-zero traffic, fall back to absolute SLO target (or mark baseline unavailable and treat as unknown / don’t rollback). Otherwise baseline compare becomes garbage.

Miles Thornton: Re paging: I’d like:
1) ticket when “breach detected but no rollback yet” (info)
2) page when “rollback executed” for enterprise/dedicated tiers OR when “rollback suppressed but breach persists”
3) page when “verdict unknown due to monitor outage” ONLY if we’re in a rollout with >X% traffic on canary (because that’s risky)

Benji Okafor: We can wire those as alert rules on `rollout_controller_rollback_total` + `rollout_controller_verdict{state="unknown"}` with labels. We already planned internal metrics for “rollback suppressed reason.”

Rafael Mendes: What cooldown number? I’m worried 30m is too short if the root cause is the new build and someone keeps pushing traffic back.

Sean Gallagher: Cooldown should be at least long enough for humans to look (and prevent automated thrash). I’d push 60m default per (tenant, route, region). Also add “manual ack” override for oncall to shorten.

Aisha Bello: +1 60m. Also rate limit pages: if auto-rollback triggers repeatedly across many tenants, we’ll page storm. Page once per incident key (route/model/region) every N minutes.

Miles Thornton: Another anti-flap guardrail: don’t re-attempt canary promotion automatically after rollback. (I know non-goal is “auto-roll forward,” just calling out that we should lock rollout state until human intervenes.)

Jordan Lee: On baseline comparison: what delta do you want as default? 20%? 30%? Needs to avoid noise.

Allison Grant: For latency, I’d start with 25% worse than baseline (p95) AND absolute threshold gate (don’t roll back if baseline already > target by a lot). For errors, 2x baseline + absolute floor (e.g., >0.5%) is good.

Rafael Mendes: Sounds like consensus:
- page on rollback executed (esp enterprise/dedicated) + on “breach persists but rollback blocked”
- introduce baseline compare + consecutive windows
- bump cooldown to 60m default
I’ll update the alerting draft + runbook language and share back. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Benji Okafor: :thumbsup: tag me when you update; I’ll make sure the controller emits the suppression reason so alerts can key off it.

Sean Gallagher: Please also add a note that thresholds are defaults not SLO commitments. We’ll need a tuning pass post-launch (expect false positives week 1).

Rafael Mendes: yep, will add “tuning plan + metrics to watch” section.
